text: In Clark and Chalmers' thought experiment, Otto (who has Alzheimer's) relies on a notebook while Inga uses her biological memory. The comparison is meant to show that:
choices: Otto's notebook is inherently unreliable and therefore cannot be cognitive
Biological memory is always epistemically superior to any external memory
Otto's notebook plays the same functional role as Inga's biological memory and so counts as part of his cognitive system
Only Inga has genuine beliefs about where the museum is
explanation: Because the notebook stores information Otto retrieves and uses to guide behavior just as Inga's memory does, the parity principle implies it is part of his cognitive system. Clark and Chalmers add three conditions (reliable availability, automatic endorsement, easy accessibility) that distinguish the notebook from, say, a library book — not a claim that external memory is inferior or that Otto lacks beliefs.
